chunks: Musa ibn al-Qasim from Ibn Abi Umayr from Hammad from al-Halabi said:
I asked Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) about the woman who circumambulates between al-Safa and al-Marwah while she is menstruating, he said: 'No'
because Allah the Exalted says: 'Indeed al-Safa and al-Marwah are among the symbols of Allah.'

key_terms.الصَّفَا وَالْمَرْوَة: Al-Safa and Al-Marwah (the two hills between which pilgrims walk)

ai.seo_question: Does a menstruating woman perform tawaf between Safa and Marwah?
ai.summary: In this narration from *Tahdhib al-Ahkam*, Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) establishes that menstruation invalidates the Sa'i ritual, grounding the ruling in the Quranic designation of al-Safa and al-Marwah as 'symbols of Allah' (2:158). This reflects the Shia scholarly view that these specific rites require the state of ritual purity (taharah) akin to prayer, distinguishing them from other Hajj acts that may be performed in a state of major impurity.
